title: Take one tissue from a pop-up box and leave the next one standing ready
instruction: Take one tissue out of the box and put it on the tray, leaving the box in place with the next tissue ready to pull.
context: Hotel and hospital housekeeping standards have attendants leave a tissue box ready: the top tissue up through the slit so the next person can take one with one hand. Pop-up tissues are interfolded, so pulling one out drags the next one's edge up through the film slit, which then holds it standing. Pulled carelessly, a light box rides up with the sheet and tips, or the next sheet comes out too. Here both tissues are real cloth soft bodies and the film is a light sprung strip; the coupling, the hold and the box's lift all come from contact friction, with no scripted rule. Unlike #531 (hold a towel roll while tearing off a sheet, then wipe), nothing is torn or wiped: one interfolded sheet is drawn out of a light box that must be held down, so friction leaves the next one presented. Unlike #1310, the pulled sheet must leave its follower behind, standing ready. Done by: maids and housekeeping cleaners (O*NET 37-2012.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. A long flat pop-up tissue box (printed paperboard, 28 x 14 x 5.5 cm, 40 g with its last sheets) lies free on the table, centred at x 28, y -2; its film slit (8 cm long, along x) is at x 28, y -10, 6 cm from the box's right end. The slit's left edge is the paperboard, its right edge a light strip of polyethylene film sprung against the sheets (about 0.14 N). The top tissue (white 2-ply paper, 7 x 7.8 cm here) stands 2.5 cm up out of the slit; inside, it bends round the leading edge of the next tissue (7 x 8.1 cm) and lies under it; the next one's edge waits just inside the slit. A grey moulded polypropylene tray (15 x 12 cm inside, 1.2 cm rim, fixed) is at x 26, y -25.
scoring: From the box's pose and the tissues' mesh node positions (on a real rig: where the box and the sheets stand in the video). Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): the box's lowest corner more than 5 mm off the table or the box tilted more than 5 deg at any step, or no node of the second tissue left inside the box under the lid (two out). Score 0 at the end if the box stands more than 1.5 cm from its spot or any node of the first tissue is still inside the box under the lid. Otherwise 0.25 (first tissue out) + 0.25 if 80 % of its nodes lie over the tray's floor and none is more than 4 cm above it + 0.5 if the second tissue's highest node stands at least 10 mm above the lid with at least a quarter of its nodes still under the lid. Halved unless both grippers are 3 cm clear of every tissue node and of the box, and the tissues (from node displacement) and the box move under 2 cm/s. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Take the second tissue back down, re-interfold the two sheets as at the start (the top one round the next one's edge, its end standing 2.5 cm up through the slit) and put the box back on its spot; empty the tray.
fidelity: Tissues: PhysX surface-deformable cloth, creased grid meshes (3 mm, ~700 nodes each), E 1 MPa, 1 mm, friction 3; density raised to 1000 kg/m3 for solver stability (5 g a sheet; real 0.3 g). Film: a 3 g strip on a sprung slider (20 N/m). No step rules. A lone sheet slips out of fully closed jaws here, so the demo pinches to a 2 mm gap. Sheets smaller than real.
